source.version: Authors' preprint in the CHI '25 template: the first page prints 2025, a 16-page ACM reference, placeholder DOI 10.1145/nnnnnnn.nnnnnnn, and placeholder ISBN. The PDF does not display an arXiv version number. The supplied citation record identifies the saved file as arXiv:2502.06197v1, submitted 2025-02-10. The ACM version of record was not used.
source.supplement_used: Appendix A, Supplementary Materials, in the same PDF, pp. 15-16: Figure 7 (embedding-similarity robustness comparison) and Table 4 (illustrative participant interaction).

studies.label: Online experiment: LLM before versus after independent ideation

counts_source.quote: We recruited a diverse group of 60 participants through Prolific1. These individuals were randomly assigned into two conditions, with 30 participants per condition.

arms.name: C_after
arms.description: Participants first generated at least three distinct supporting ideas independently, then could reveal the GPT-4 component to supplement or expand their ideas. The Display AI button was initially disabled and became available after ideas were saved (PDF pp. 3-4, Sections 3.3-3.4.1).

arms.name: C_before
arms.description: GPT-4 idea-generation component available from the beginning and visible throughout the ideation task, with no prerequisite independent ideation (PDF pp. 3-4, Sections 3.3-3.4.1).

studies.task: Generate as many supporting ideas as possible for one of two counterbalanced health-related claims, using existing knowledge and logical reasoning without requiring factual correctness (PDF p. 3, Sections 3.1 and 3.3).

ai_tool.name: OpenAI GPT-4 API in a custom web application
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 3, Section 3.4 and footnote 7; editable prompts and generated ideas described on PDF pp. 4-5, Sections 3.4.1-3.4.2. Model release year and exact GPT-4 snapshot are not printed.

preregistration.where: No preregistration is stated in the supplied article or Appendix A.

estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Authors counted distinct supporting ideas submitted by each participant, including independently generated and LLM-assisted ideas; redundant or repetitive ideas were excluded. The number of coders, blinding, and distinctness adjudication rules are not stated (PDF p. 5, Section 3.5.2).

sources.quote: Generating ideas with LLM from the start (𝐶𝑏𝑒𝑓𝑜𝑟𝑒) led par- ticipants to write slightly fewer supporting ideas (𝑀= 3.867;𝑆𝐷= 2.285) compared to the 𝐶𝑎𝑓𝑡𝑒𝑟condition (𝑀= 5.567;𝑆𝐷= 4.345).

sources.locator: PDF p. 7, Section 4.1, Student t-test of idea quantity
sources.quote: marginal effect on the number of supporting ideas participants gen- erated in the study (𝑡(58) = −1.897, 𝑝= 0.063,𝑑= −0.490)

estimates.notes: AI was available during the final ideation task, but C_after combines ideas first written independently with ideas added or edited after AI access. The outcome is with_ai; no AI-removal outcome was measured (PDF pp. 3-4, Sections 3.3-3.4.1). The paper prints assignment counts but no analysis-specific participant counts; n_treatment, n_control, and n_total are null rather than inferred from degrees of freedom or the absence of reported exclusions. Independent Student t-test. The printed t and d use C_before minus C_after, opposite to the named treatment-minus-control contrast; their signs are preserved without conversion. The standardizer for d is not defined. The paper calls the result marginal and Table 3 repeats that interpretation (PDF p. 11). This is the main unadjusted comparison; the SEM direct path is a separate record from the same participants. C_after required independent ideas before unlocking AI (PDF p. 3, Section 3.3).

estimates.outcome: Similarity between participant ideas and LLM-generated ideas (TF-IDF)
estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: After stop-word removal, stemming or lemmatization, and lowercasing, TF-IDF vectors were compared by cosine similarity between each participant idea and each LLM idea that participant received. Each participant idea was represented by its vector of similarities to the LLM ideas; vector magnitudes were averaged to obtain one participant score. Section 3.5.3 describes this pipeline; Table 1 calls the magnitude the magnitude of the TF-IDF vector, so implementation wording is ambiguous. The measure is not simply the mean pairwise cosine similarity (PDF pp. 5-6, Section 3.5.3 and Table 1).

sources.quote: Specifically, participants in the 𝐶𝑏𝑒𝑓𝑜𝑟𝑒condition had a higher sim- ilarity score (𝑀= 0.899;𝑆𝐷= 0.404) than in the 𝐶𝑎𝑓𝑡𝑒𝑟condition (𝑀= 0.648;𝑆𝐷= 0.250),

sources.locator: PDF p. 7, Section 4.1, Welch t-test of similarity with LLM ideas

estimates.notes: AI was available during the final ideation task, but C_after combines ideas first written independently with ideas added or edited after AI access. The outcome is with_ai; no AI-removal outcome was measured (PDF pp. 3-4, Sections 3.3-3.4.1). The paper prints assignment counts but no analysis-specific participant counts; n_treatment, n_control, and n_total are null rather than inferred from degrees of freedom or the absence of reported exclusions. Welch t-test. The reported t = 4.778 is transcribed exactly, despite the inconsistency flagged in the reconciled screening form between this t and the other printed statistics. It must not be used to derive an effect or uncertainty without resolution. No corrected t has been substituted. The printed t and d run C_before minus C_after; their signs are preserved. The standardizer for d is not stated. Higher scores indicate more overlap with AI suggestions, and the authors interpret lower scores as more original or independent ideas (PDF p. 5, Section 3.5.3). Construct other follows the screening form: this compares a person with AI suggestions, not different people. The embedding robustness variant and the SEM direct path are separate records on this same sample.

estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: OpenAI text-embedding-ada-002 embeddings of each idea; cosine similarities across unique pairs within one participant’s idea set, excluding self-pairs; score defined as 1 minus average similarity. This is variation within a person, coded flexibility, rather than across-people diversity (PDF p. 5, Section 3.5.4).

sources.locator: PDF p. 7, Section 4.1, Welch t-test of participant idea diversity
sources.quote: Welch t-test showed that there was no significant difference be- tween different timings of LLM usage (𝑡(36.472) = 1.337, 𝑝= 0.189,𝑑= 0.345).

estimates.notes: AI was available during the final ideation task, but C_after combines ideas first written independently with ideas added or edited after AI access. The outcome is with_ai; no AI-removal outcome was measured (PDF pp. 3-4, Sections 3.3-3.4.1). The paper prints assignment counts but no analysis-specific participant counts; n_treatment, n_control, and n_total are null rather than inferred from degrees of freedom or the absence of reported exclusions. Welch t-test. Higher means more semantic variation among one participant’s own ideas. Within-person describes the outcome construction, not a within-person randomized design: assignment was between people, so within_person is null. The paper prints no arm means, SDs, raw difference, or confidence interval; Figure 3(c) shows distributions without numeric arm summaries (PDF p. 8). No values were read from the figure. The sign convention for the printed t and d, and the standardizer for d, are not stated. The reported positive signs are retained without assuming the direction of C_after minus C_before. This outcome was omitted from the SEM because it was not significant (PDF p. 9, footnote 11).

regression.model: Structural equation model, outcome regressed on LLM Usage Timing, Creative Self Efficacy, Autonomy, and Ownership (PDF p. 11, Table 2). Confidence intervals use bootstrap resampling with 1000 samples (PDF p. 9, Section 4.3.2). The paper does not state the SE estimator or a standardization of the outcome.

sources.quote: we built a Structural Equation Model (SEM) using bootstrap resampling with 1000 sam- ples to estimate the 95% confidence intervals.

estimates.notes: AI was available during the final ideation task, but C_after combines ideas first written independently with ideas added or edited after AI access. The outcome is with_ai; no AI-removal outcome was measured (PDF pp. 3-4, Sections 3.3-3.4.1). The paper prints assignment counts but no analysis-specific participant counts; n_treatment, n_control, and n_total are null rather than inferred from degrees of freedom or the absence of reported exclusions. This is the direct timing path conditional on post-treatment creative self-efficacy, autonomy, and ownership, not the unadjusted total contrast. It is recorded separately to avoid combining the SEM z-test and p-value with the main t-test. The numeric coding of LLM Usage Timing is not specified; its orientation is inferred from the authors’ interpretation that delayed access increases autonomy (PDF p. 9, Section 4.3.2) and reduces similarity (PDF p. 10, Section 4.3.2). Table 2 labels the coefficient Estimate and describes no outcome standardization; it is recorded as raw, not beta_std. The bootstrap resampling unit is not specified; the analysis uses one outcome and one set of questionnaire scores per participant. The confidence interval is for the adjusted raw timing coefficient. Reporting discrepancy: the printed p = 0.084 and bootstrap 95% CI [0.120, 3.210] differ on whether zero is excluded at the nominal level. Both are retained as printed; Table 2 does not highlight this timing path as significant.

estimates.measure_detail: Same participant-to-LLM similarity pipeline as the TF-IDF analysis, replacing TF-IDF vectors with OpenAI text-embedding-ada-002 embeddings while keeping the other steps unchanged (PDF p. 5, footnote 8). One score per participant; Appendix A, Figure 7 compares the two conditions.

The appendix reports a significant difference and describes C_after scores as concentrated at lower similarity values, but supplies no numerical arm means, SDs, difference, test statistic, exact p-value, effect size, or confidence interval in text. open_items: The document prints the recruitment and assignment counts but does not explicitly print analysis-specific totals or per-arm analyzed counts. Study and arm n_analyzed and estimate n_treatment/n_control/n_total are null. The screening form inferred analyzed counts from assignment, absence of stated exclusions, and degrees of freedom; that inference is not transcribed under the extraction rule (PDF p. 3, Section 3.2; PDF p. 7, Section 4.1).

The printed Welch t-statistic for TF-IDF similarity is flagged as inconsistent in the screening form. It is retained as printed for provenance and must not supply a derived effect or uncertainty until resolved against a corrected version or author clarification (PDF p. 7, Section 4.1).

For within-person idea diversity, numeric arm means and SDs are not printed; the sign convention of t and d is not stated. The standardizer used for the reported d values is not defined for any of the main output comparisons (PDF p. 7, Section 4.1; PDF p. 8, Figure 3).

LLM Usage Timing coding is not specified in the SEM. The direction recorded for the configurations follows the prose interpretation. The outcome standardization and precise SE estimator are not explicitly identified; bootstrap confidence intervals are described, without specifying the resampling unit (PDF pp. 9-11, Section 4.3.2 and Table 2).
For the quantity SEM timing path, the printed p-value and bootstrap confidence interval give different significance conclusions. Both are preserved exactly (PDF p. 11, Table 2).

The number of LLM-generated ideas received per arm is not reported. Since the similarity score uses vector magnitudes, the interpretation may depend on the number of AI suggestions. The prose and pseudocode differ in how they name the vector whose magnitude is calculated (PDF pp. 5-6, Section 3.5.3 and Table 1).

The embedding-similarity robustness comparison supplies only graphical distributions and a qualitative significance statement; numeric arm levels and uncertainty cannot be transcribed (PDF p. 15, Appendix A, Figure 7).
GPT-4 release year, exact model snapshot, participant countries, and preregistration are not stated in the supplied document; no external values are substituted.
The saved document is a preprint with placeholder publication identifiers. The supplied citation record identifies a later ACM version of record, which was not compared for corrections.
notes: Extracted by A on 2026-10-10 from the complete supplied markdown and checked against extracted PDF text for every cited page. Reconciliation and verification remain pending. There is one randomized sample and one AI-design contrast; repeated outcome and model records share participants. The main tests and the SEM direct paths are separate specifications, with the main tests representing the unadjusted comparisons. No primary outcome or preregistration is stated. None of the outcomes measures similarity across different people or unassisted performance after AI removal. All stats values are transcribed without calculation or sign reversal. Quotes retain printed numeric precision and PDF-extracted symbols; whitespace is collapsed, and PDF line-break hyphenation is preserved. No values are estimated from figures. Analysis-specific sample sizes are not inferred from the screening form. The illustrative interaction in Appendix A, Table 4 is not an additional full-sample comparison.
